The '''Virtual International Authority File''' ('''VIAF''') is an international [[authority file]]. It is a joint project of several national libraries, operated by the [[OCLC|Online Computer Library Center]] (OCLC).<ref name="LibraryJournal-VIAFtoOCLC">{{Cite journal |last1=Kelley |first1=Michael |last2=Schwartz |first2=Meredith |year=2012 |title=VIAF service transitions to OCLC |journal=[[Library Journal]] |publisher=[[Media Source Inc.]] |volume=137 |issue=8 |page=16}}&nbsp;{{closed access}}</ref>

== History ==
[[File:VIAF Screenshot 2012.png|thumb|[[Homepage]] in 2012]]
Discussions about having a joint international authority started in the late 1990s. After several failed attempts to develop a unique joint authority file, the new idea was to link existing national authorities. This would present all the benefits of a standard file without requiring a significant investment of time and expense in the process.<ref name="IFLA-VIAF-Origins-2016">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VC4Gt5xXLzo |title=VIAF: Origins |date=12 August 2016 |last=O'Neill |first=Edward T. |publisher=[[OCLC]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713143859/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VC4Gt5xXLzo |archive-date=2018-07-13 |format=Video presentation |via=YouTube |website=Authority Data on the Web, a Satellite Meeting of the 2016 [[International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions|IFLA]] World Library and Information Congress}}</ref>

The project was initiated by the American [[Library of Congress]] (LC), the [[German National Library]] (DNB), and the OCLC in April 1998 as a proof-of-concept that authority records can be linked.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 December 2019 |title=VIAF: Convenient access to name authority files |url=https://www.oclc.org/en/viaf.html |website=OCLC}}</ref> After extensive testing, the VIAF consortium was formed at the 2003 World Library and Information Congress, hosted by the [[International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions|International Federation of Library Associations]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Loesch |first=Martha Fallahay |date=2011-02-28 |title=The Virtual International Authority File |journal=Technical Services Quarterly |language=en |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=255–256 |doi=10.1080/07317131.2011.546304 |issn=0731-7131 |s2cid=62694070}}</ref> on 6 August 2003,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morris |first=Susan R. |date=September 2003 |title=Virtual International Authority |url=https://www.loc.gov/loc/lcib/0309/authority.html |access-date=2021-01-05 |website=Library of Congress Information Bulletin |publisher=[[Library of Congress]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Agnew |first=Grace |title=Digital Rights Management: A Librarian's Guide to Technology and Practise |publisher=[[Woodhead Publishing|Chandos Publishing]] |year=2008 |isbn=978-1-84334-125-3 |page=[[iarchive:digitalrightsman0000agne o4q5/page/180/mode/1up|180]] |oclc=62715356}}</ref> and by September it had its own page at the OCLC website.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 September 2003 |title=Virtual international authority file [OCLC - Projects] |url=http://www.oclc.org/research/projects/viaf/default.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030921104347/http://www.oclc.org/research/projects/viaf/default.htm |archive-date=21 September 2003}}</ref> The {{lang|fr|[[Bibliothèque nationale de France]]|italic=no}} (BnF) joined the project on 5 October 2007.

The project transitioned to being a service of OCLC on 4 April 2012.<ref name="OCLC-VIAF-Service-2012">{{Cite press release |title=Virtual International Authority File service transitions to OCLC; contributing institutions continue to shape direction through VIAF Council |date=4 April 2012 |location=[[Dublin, Ohio|Dublin, OH]] |url=http://www.oclc.org/en/news/releases/2012/201224.html |language=en |last=Murphy |first=Bob |website=[[OCLC]]}}</ref>

The aim is to link the national authority files (such as the German [[Integrated Authority File]]) to a single virtual authority file. In this file, identical records from the different data sets are linked together. A VIAF record receives a standard data number, contains the primary "see" and "see also" records from the original documents, and refers to the original authority records. The data is made available online and is available for research and, data exchange and sharing. Reciprocal updating uses the [[Open Archives Initiative]] [[Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting|Protocol for Metadata Harvesting]] (OAI-PMH) protocol.

The file numbers are also being added to [[Wikipedia]] biographical articles and are incorporated into [[Wikidata]].<ref name="OCLC-VIAFbot-2012">{{Cite news |last1=Klein |first1=Max |last2=Renspie |first2=Melissa |date=7 December 2012 |title=VIAFbot Edits 250,000 Wikipedia Articles to Reciprocate All Links from VIAF into Wikipedia |url=http://www.oclc.org/research/news/2012/12-07a.html |work=[[OCLC]]}}</ref><ref name="Code4Lib-VIAFbot-2013">{{Cite journal |last1=Klein |first1=Maximilian |last2=Kyrios |first2=Alex |date=14 October 2013 |title=VIAFbot and the Integration of Library Data on Wikipedia |url=http://journal.code4lib.org/articles/8964 |journal=The Code4Lib Journal |issue=22 |issn=1940-5758}}</ref>

[[Christine L. Borgman]] groups VIAF with the [[International Standard Name Identifier]] and [[ORCID]] systems, describing all three as "loosely coordinated efforts to standardize name forms".{{Sfn |Borgman |2015 |p=260}} Borgman characterizes all three systems as attempts to solve the problem of [[author name disambiguation]], which has grown in scale as the quantity of [[data]] multiplies.{{Sfn |Borgman |2015 |p=260}} She notes that VIAF, unlike the other two systems, is led by libraries, as opposed to individual authors or creators.{{Sfn |Borgman |2015 |p=260}}

== VIAF clusters ==
VIAF's clustering algorithm is run every month.  As more data are added from participating libraries, clusters of authority records may coalesce or split, leading to some fluctuation in the VIAF identifier of certain authority records.<ref name="DLib-VIAF-Ambiguity-2014">{{Cite journal |last1=Hickey |first1=Thomas B. |last2=Toves |first2=Jenny A. |date=July 2014 |title=Managing Ambiguity In VIAF |url=http://www.dlib.org/dlib/july14/hickey/07hickey.html |journal=[[D-Lib Magazine]] |publisher=[[Corporation for National Research Initiatives]] |volume=20 |issue=7/8 |doi=10.1045/july2014-hickey |doi-access=free}}</ref>
